data.body: The pre-commit ruff (check + format) keeps regressing because merges land before the ruff-format is clean at the merge point, so a git push on the primary fails. Make ruff a merge-enforced concern: default/configure [ci].command to run `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` before merge and auto-fix (ruff check --fix / ruff format) with the corrections recorded, so a changed file cannot merge with lint drift. Regression test: a branch with ruff drift is refused/auto-corrected by the ci gate before merge.
data.title: make ruff check+format a merge-enforced ci gate (auto-fix) per project: add ruff to [ci].command before merge, with correction of any issues it finds

data.claim: superseded_by with no paths falls back to ancestry alone and returns True for ANY descendant commit, including one touching only .ddflow/events; the fix makes the no-paths case read the diff and supersede only when a non-bookkeeping source file changed.
data.falsifier: A phase-scoped superseded_by call (paths=None) over a commit that changed only .ddflow/events must return False; the regression test that would refute the fix asserts not superseded_by(began, now, cwd) for an event-only commit.
data.mechanism: evidence.py superseded_by: when  is empty it returns True before asking git which files changed; a phase item has no globs, so  is None and even a .ddflow/events-only commit advances ancestry and supersedes the run.
data.probe_output: FAILED on unfixed code: AssertionError: assert not True (event-only commit superseded). PASSED after the fix (5 passed with test_gate_supersede_content.py).
data.question: Does superseded_by treat an event-only commit as superseding a phase gate run (which has no globs)?
